segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Welcome to Psalm Nights. [pause 16]

Let the lights go down. Let your shoulders go down with them. [pause 19]

Tonight we read the first part of Psalm 34. David wrote it after a frightening escape, when he had to pretend to be out of his mind to get away. And afterward, he sang. [pause 18]

We will read it twice. [pause 21]

verses.text: A Psalm of David, when he changed his behaviour before Abimelech; who drove him away, and he departed. I will bless the LORD at all times: his praise shall continually be in my mouth.
My soul shall make her boast in the LORD: the humble shall hear thereof, and be glad.
O magnify the LORD with me, and let us exalt his name together.
I sought the LORD, and he heard me, and delivered me from all my fears.
They looked unto him, and were lightened: and their faces were not ashamed.
This poor man cried, and the LORD heard him, and saved him out of all his troubles.
The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.
O taste and see that the LORD is good: blessed is the man that trusteth in him.
O fear the LORD, ye his saints: for there is no want to them that fear him.
The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger: but they that seek the LORD shall not want any good thing.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Bless the Lord, at all times. At all times. Not only when the day went well. [pause 31]

He sought the Lord, and was heard. David is not giving a lecture here. He is telling what happened to him. I looked for God, and God answered. [pause 31]

The angel of the Lord encamps around those who fear him. Encamps. Like a tent pitched around you for the night. [pause 31]

O taste and see. Faith is not only something you think. It is something you can taste, like bread, like water when you are thirsty. [pause 35]

Two more verses from later in the same psalm. [pause 29]

verses.text: The righteous cry, and the LORD heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.
The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
Near to the brokenhearted. If your heart is broken tonight, he is not far. He is nearer than you think. [pause 33]

Here is the beginning of Psalm 34 again. Let it taste like something good. [pause 35]

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text:
That is all for tonight. [pause 8]

Let the quiet come in like a tide. Slowly. No hurry. [pause 12]

Your work is done for today. What is left can wait for the light. [pause 12]

If you are still awake a while, that is all right. Lie still and let the words you heard be near you. [pause 15]

He knows your name. He knows this night. [pause 20]

Rest. [pause 45]

first_reader.note: Written by Claude in the landing session, then Claude's pastor and cultural read.

pastor.note: Stored KJV pasted by code; short echoes only. Each night keeps its psalm's own point (contentment, tasting God's goodness, remembering benefits, night watches, honest sadness, the higher rock, longing for God's house, our short days, return to rest, surrounded like Jerusalem). Psalm 103's 'healeth' told as memory of who God has been, not a promise; Psalm 42 points a long sadness to a pastor, a doctor or a friend; no sleep or safety promise in the new rests.

cultural.note: Plain English for a tired listener; grief and low nights named without pity; two new shared rests so closes vary; pacing by silence only (13.5-13.7 min voiced at the measured 117 wpm).
